tips.title: Word order
tips.text: The verb always comes last in a Korean sentence: subject, object, verb.

tips.title: Topic particle 은/는
tips.text: 은/는 marks what the sentence is about. Use 는 after a vowel and 은 after a consonant.

tips.title: Subject particle 이/가
tips.text: 이/가 marks the subject, often with 있어요 (there is / to have). Use 가 after a vowel and 이 after a consonant.

tips.title: Object particle 을/를
tips.text: 을/를 marks the object, the thing the action is done to. Use 를 after a vowel and 을 after a consonant.

tips.title: 에 or 에서?
tips.text: 에 marks where you are going or where something is. 에서 marks where an action happens.

tips.title: "To be": 예요/이에요
tips.text: Add 예요 after a word that ends in a vowel and 이에요 after a word that ends in a consonant.

tips.title: Polite present tense
tips.text: Remove 다 from the verb. If the last vowel is ㅏ or ㅗ, add 아요. Otherwise add 어요. 하다 verbs become 해요.

tips.title: Polite past tense
tips.text: Remove 다 from the verb. If the last vowel is ㅏ or ㅗ, add 았어요. Otherwise add 었어요. 하다 verbs become 했어요.
